prompt.context: Your client today is a global specialty retailer of children's toys and baby products with annual worldwide revenues totaling over $11 BN. After a recent buyout by Private Equity, the firm has been pursuing aggressive growth targets across all three of its divisions. The e-commerce division has about $400 MM in total revenue and a major area of growth has been identified within Shipping & Handling (S&H) of customer orders. Your client offers its customers two S&H options: '2nd Day Expedited' or 'Ground', and each of those are further divided into 'Lower 48 States' or 'Alaska & Hawaii' depending on the order destination zip code. Annual S&H revenue from each product offering is as follows: Ground to Lower 48: $32 MM; Ground to AK & HI: $180 K; Expedited to Lower 48: $3.73 MM; Expedited to AK & HI: $90 K.
prompt.question: The e-commerce division hopes to increase S&H profits by approximately 115%. You are part of the team studying their S&H economics. Make a recommendation to impact immediate growth and meet their goals.

clarifying_info.q: How is total e-commerce revenue broken down?
clarifying_info.a: Total revenue = $400 MM. S&H Revenue = 9% ($36 MM); Merchandise Sales Revenue = 91% ($364 MM).

clarifying_info.q: Where does the client ship from?
clarifying_info.a: The client ships all orders from a single distribution center in Groveport, OH.

clarifying_info.q: How many box sizes does the client use?
clarifying_info.a: The client ships products in 8 different box sizes.

21% of orders include SKUs with fixed S&H prices (same price regardless of destination). 73% of orders are priced against a weight table. 6% of orders include a mix of fixed-price and weight-table items.

clarifying_info.q: What is the weight table pricing structure?
clarifying_info.a: Ground to Lower 48: $4.84 for first 1 lb, +$0.85 per additional lb. Ground to AK & HI: $6.84 for first 1 lb, +$0.85 per additional lb. 2nd Day to Lower 48: $10.98 for first 1 lb, +$0.99 per additional lb. 2nd Day to AK & HI: $20.98 for first 1 lb, +$0.99 per additional lb. This is a blended price aggregating the carrier's zone-based cost table with a 25% markup.

clarifying_info.q: How does the vendor charge the client?
clarifying_info.a: The vendor charges based on: (1) Distance — Lower 48 divided into 8 zones (1=closest, 8=furthest); AK & HI into 2 zones (Metro and Remote). (2) Size — small packages (<3 cubic feet) billed by weight; large items billed by volumetric dimensions.

clarifying_info.q: How are the client's prices compared to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: The client is currently priced on par with competitors.

exhibits.title: Business Shipped to Various Segments
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing total merchandise shipped vs. merchandise shipped at a loss across seven segments: Ground-L48, Ground-AK&HI, 2nd Day-L48, 2nd Day-AK&HI, Weight Table, Fixed Pricing, and Weight & Fixed Price.

exhibits.title: Gross Margin on Category Wins and Losses
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing gross margin on winners (positive) and gross margin on losses (negative) for each of seven segments: Ground-L48, Ground-AK&HI, 2nd Day-L48, 2nd Day-AK&HI, Weight Table, Fixed Pricing, and Weight & Fixed Price.

framework: Understand the revenue structure: four S&H product offerings (Ground vs. Expedited x Lower 48 vs. AK&HI) plus fixed vs. weight-table pricing
Analyze cost structure: carrier charges by zone-distance and package size/volume; single DC in Ohio
Identify loss-making segments using exhibit data (margin on wins vs. losses by category)
Quantify the business at risk if prices are raised on loss-making segments
Quantify the percentage of total losses that can be saved by targeting specific segments
Distinguish short-term (pricing) from long-term (cost reduction) levers
Formulate a recommendation that achieves the ~115% profit improvement target

questions.prompt: Examine Exhibit 1. What does it tell you about where losses are concentrated across the four shipping product categories?
questions.guidance: Approximately 1/3 (~28%) of total business is shipped at a loss. ~78% of all business to Alaska & Hawaii (both Ground and 2nd Day) is shipped at a loss. ~34% of all fixed-price orders are shipped at a loss. Ground to Lower 48 dominates total volume but a meaningful share ships at a loss.

questions.prompt: Examine Exhibit 2. Calculate the gross margin percentage for each of the four S&H product categories (Ground-L48, Ground-AK&HI, 2nd Day-L48, 2nd Day-AK&HI).
questions.guidance: Margin formula: (Margin on Wins + Margin on Losses) / Total Revenue in Category. The key insight is that AK&HI and Expedited categories run deeply negative margins.

math.setup: Margin = (Gross Margin on Winners + Gross Margin on Losses) / Total S&H Revenue in category
math.answer: Ground L48: +13%; Ground AK&HI: -142%; 2nd Day L48: -17%; 2nd Day AK&HI: -39%

questions.prompt: The largest loss bucket is Ground shipments to the Lower 48. Why should the client NOT raise prices there, but SHOULD raise prices on the other three S&H offerings?
questions.guidance: Ground L48 is ~91% of business; raising prices risks meaningfully reducing demand for merchandise and orders — too large to risk. Expedited is a premium product with likely lower price elasticity. AK&HI is less than 1% of total business but contributes ~5% of losses — no strategic reason to subsidize it.

questions.prompt: The client's S&H prices average 25% above the vendor's cost table, yet there are egregious losses in certain categories. What explains this, and what is the longer-term fix?
questions.guidance: The primary driver is 'over-boxing': items whose manufacturer packaging is not durable for cargo shipping must be placed in a larger outer box, increasing the billed weight and/or volumetric dimensions beyond what the 25% markup compensates for. The fix requires a carton-size study to determine the optimal assortment of box sizes relative to order mix.

questions.prompt: If the client raises prices on AK&HI (Ground and 2nd Day), Expedited to Lower 48, and the 44 high-loss fixed-price SKUs, what percentage of total merchandise dollars are at risk?
questions.guidance: Compute merchandise dollars in each targeted segment, sum them, and divide by total merchandise revenue ($364 MM). Answer is approximately 10.89%.

math.setup: % at risk = (Merch to AK&HI + Merch to Expedited L48 + Merch in 10% fixed-price items) / Total Merchandise Dollars
steps: Merch to AK&HI Ground + 2nd Day (from Exhibit 1): ~$1,800K + $200K = $2,000K
44 fixed-price SKUs = 10% of fixed-price merchandise. Fixed Pricing total merch ≈ $76,440K (from Exhibit 1); 10% = $7,644K
math.answer: Approximately 10.89% of total merchandise dollars are at risk

questions.prompt: What percentage of total losses can be saved by raising prices on the three targeted segments (AK&HI, Expedited L48, and the 44 fixed-price SKUs)?
questions.guidance: Sum the losses in AK&HI (both modes), Expedited L48, and 59% of fixed-price losses (attributable to the 44 items). Divide by total losses across all categories.

math.setup: % loss saved = (Loss AK&HI + Loss Expedited L48 + 59% x Loss Fixed Pricing) / Total Losses
steps: Loss Ground AK&HI: $257.2K; Loss 2nd Day AK&HI: $38.18K; Loss 2nd Day L48: $1,010K
math.answer: Approximately 29.68% (~30%) of total losses can be saved

questions.prompt: Should raising prices be a long-term solution? Why or why not?
questions.guidance: No. Raising prices leaves the client at a competitive disadvantage (currently priced on par with competitors). Long-term goal must be cost reduction. Specific long-term levers: carton-size study to optimize box assortment; expand distribution network with east and west coast DCs to reduce zone distances and carrier costs; negotiate lower rates with the single shipping vendor.

brainstorming.prompt: What other shipping cost drivers should the client investigate per order, beyond distance and package size?

categories.name: Order Consolidation
ideas: Number of shipments per order — large orders with smaller items may ship in fewer boxes ('combinable'). More boxes = more carrier charges
Item dimensions vs. box assortment — mismatch leads to sending a large box for a small item, inflating volumetric billing

categories.name: Packaging Factors
ideas: 'Over-boxing' — manufacturer packaging not durable for cargo shipping requires an outer box, increasing billed weight and dimensions
8 box sizes may be insufficient to match item dimensions, forcing systematic over-boxing

categories.name: Network / Logistics
ideas: Single DC in Ohio means long zone distances to west coast (Zone 7-8) and AK&HI, driving up carrier costs
No redundancy in the network — all volume flows through one node

recommendation: Short-term: Raise S&H prices on (a) Ground and 2nd Day shipments to AK & HI, (b) 2nd Day Expedited shipments to Lower 48, and (c) the 44 fixed-price SKUs that generate 59% of fixed-price losses. This targets ~11% of merchandise dollars and can recover ~30% of current S&H losses.

Long-term: Do not rely on higher prices as a permanent fix — it erodes competitive position. Focus on cost reduction: conduct a carton-size study to optimize the box assortment; expand the distribution network with east and west coast DCs to reduce carrier zone distances; renegotiate shipping rates with the single delivery vendor.
risks: Raising prices on the ~11% of at-risk merchandise could reduce demand and order volumes in those segments
AK&HI price increases could damage brand presence in those markets if the client has strategic reasons to serve them
Higher prices on Expedited shipping may reduce its usage, indirectly affecting customer satisfaction and loyalty
Single-vendor dependency limits negotiating leverage and introduces supply-chain concentration risk
next_steps: Conduct a detailed carton-size study: analyze item dimensions, demand volumes, and most frequent item combinations to determine the optimal box assortment
Model the demand elasticity impact of price increases in targeted segments before implementation
Evaluate cost-benefit of opening east and west coast distribution centers
Issue an RFP or negotiate with the existing carrier to secure better zone-based rates
Monitor S&H profit margins quarterly against the 115% improvement target
